title: What is Trial-to-Paid Conversion? Formula & Benchmarks
meta_description: Trial-to-paid conversion is the share of trial starters who pay. The formula, the category and regional medians, and why India runs at 15.2%.

visuals.alt: Median trial-to-paid conversion by trial length and by region, each row carrying its source and the date it was verified
visuals.caption: Medians from RevenueCat's 2026 report, verified 30 September 2026.

faq.q: What is a good trial-to-paid conversion rate?
faq.a: Compare against your category, not the overall median. Travel sits at 43.5% and Photo & Video at 22.2%, and that gap is wider than most teams move their own number in a year.

faq.q: How long should a free trial be?
faq.a: Longer converts better in the data: 42.5% median for 17 to 32 days against 25.5% for four days or fewer. The long trial buys enough sessions for the product to prove itself.

faq.q: Why is trial-to-paid conversion lower in India?
faq.a: The regional median is 15.2% against 34.2% in North America. Prices sit at 0.6 times the US baseline, and card recurring fails more often than UPI Autopay, which runs at 92% or better.

unique_value_statement: Carries the IN/SEA regional median of 15.2% alongside the 0.6x India price index and UPI Autopay mandate success, which the ranking pages omit entirely — they quote the global median and stop.
